To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the removal of a fucose residue from oligosaccharide side chains attached to Asn 297 of human IgG1 results in a significant increase in ADCC via enhanced Fc gamma RIIIa binding, and that this enhancement is attributed to subtle conformational change of the Fc fragment.

the overall structures of the fucosyalted and nonfucosyalted Fc fragments were found to be similar, but the electron density maps of the fucysolated and nonfucysolated Fc fragments were both different from the previously reported isomophous Fc crystals.
the overall structures of the fuc- and nonfuc-Fc fragments were very similar, but a subtle difference in hydration mode around Tyr 296 was detected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural comparison of fucysylated and non-fucosylated IgG1-Fcs.
the structural basis of glycoform-dependent enhancement of IgG1 binding affinity for FcgammaRIIIa.
the structural basis for glycoform-dependent Fc functions and provides the first structural evidence for the existence of multiple conformations of IgG1 in crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fucosylation of oligosaccharide at Asn297 of the Fc domain of IgG1 does not affect its overall conformation, but the fucosidation of the oligosacchride does alter the hydration mode around Tyr 296, resulting in the enhancement of ADCC activity.
there is no structural difference between the fucosylation and nonfucosyation of the oligosacchride at Asn297 of IgG1.
the fucose residue of the oligosacchardies attached to Asn 297 of IgG1 is not a structural determinant of IgG1 binding affinity to FcgammaR IIIa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the crystal structures of Fc are sensitive to the presence of the fucose moiety in the oligosac-charide attached to Asn 297, and the crystal structures of nonfucos-ylated Fc and fucosyl-ated Fc are similar to each other but different from the crystal structures of previously reported Fc.

a single glycoform of IgG1 is able to adopt multiple conformations, and that the fucosylation state of the oligosaccharyl moiety is one of the factors that determines the conformational preference of the IgG1 Fc fragment.
the fucosylation of the oligosaccharyl chain at Asn297 is not the only determinant of the IgG1-FcgammaRIIIa interaction, but that the overall IgG1 conformation is also important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallographic packing of Fc fragments in the crystal lattices can be significantly different depending on the presence/absence of fucose.
the crystallographic packing of Fc molecules in the crystals is not the same as the molecular packing in solution, and that the packing in the crystals is dependent on the glycoform.
the conformation of the Fc fragment is sensitive to the crystallization conditions and that the structural information obtained from Fc crystals must be carefully interpreted.
